analysis:
MARKET & PORTFOLIO OVERVIEW: SPY is in a confirmed uptrend (+3.3% vs SMA50, positive slope), which is constructive. However, the portfolio is already at 94% deployment with only ~$1,060 of headroom for new buys — far too little to size any new position properly (minimum useful entry on a $103k book would be ~$10k-15k). Forcing a trade into a $1,060 slot is not discipline; it is noise. The historical profit factor of 0.55x (losing money net across 15 trades) and negative Sortino of -1.40 reinforce that this cycle's priority is capital preservation and letting existing winners run — NOT manufacturing new activity.

EXISTING POSITION REVIEW:
• A (+14.3%): Strong gain. Agilent is not in today's screened list — worth watching whether it failed trend filter in a future cycle — but the position is profitable and there is no thesis-break signal yet. Hold.
• AMP (+5.0%): Solid performer in an uptrend, quality financial. Hold.
• LMT (+6.1%): Defense thesis intact, basing in uptrend. Hold.
• TEL (-0.4%): Appears on today's screened candidate list as UPTREND/basing with solid rev growth (+13.8%) and positive EPS revisions. Flat performance is within noise; no thesis break. Hold.
• MCO (+1.4%): FLAGGED — Moody's does NOT appear in today's screened candidates list (30 names that passed quality + no-confirmed-downtrend filters). Given MCO is clearly a quality business (ROE, margins, moat), the likely failure is the trend filter — suggesting MCO may now be in a confirmed downtrend or deteriorating tape. At only +1.42% gain, the risk/reward of continuing to hold a position that likely failed trend screening is asymmetric to the downside. Recommend monitoring closely; if MCO breaks below its SMA50 or fails to recapture it within 2-3 weeks, exit to protect capital and free ~$12k for a better-setup candidate. Do NOT sell into this session without confirming trend deterioration — a forced sell on a +1.4% position without price confirmation is also wrong.

NEW TRADES: ZERO. The capacity constraint alone disqualifies new entries. Even the best candidate (e.g., BR or IDXX basing setups) cannot be sized to 1-2% equity risk with $1,060 available. Beyond capacity: several high-ranking candidates (IT, WDAY, CTSH) are already +19-22% above SMA50, which violates the 'not extended' rule. FDS earnings in 35 days create binary risk. DG and WDAY both have earnings in 14 days — untradeable per thesis. The right answer is patience. Protecting the 94% already deployed and waiting for a natural exit (target hit or stop hit on an existing position) before adding is the disciplined move. Cash is a position. A quiet book in this regime is a success.
